summary: Stream resume suppressed when client IP affinity changes during long SSE/ws generation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that long-running streaming responses (SSE and websocket) intermittently stop emitting the final closing tokens/paragraph when the client's apparent source IP changes mid-stream (observed during mobile carrier handoffs and corporate proxy rebinds). The stream appears to resume (client reconnect succeeds) but the final terminal chunk or closing metadata is missing, leaving partial output and a perpetually open client state.

Impact:
- Several TextFlow.ai jobs observed truncated summaries in ~2-4% of long streaming sessions (>= 60s).
- Affects user-facing text generation features (document summaries, long chat responses) for the customer; customers report incorrect UX (missing last paragraph).
- Customer is on a Dedicated plan; issue escalated because production traffic is impacted.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east-1 (redwood-dedicated-us-east-4).
- Affected app: TextFlow.ai ingestion pipeline using streaming SSE for incremental updates.
- Observed on both SSE and websocket transports.
- Upstream load balancer: customer-facing ALB with source NAT and short session affinity cookie (60s).

Steps to reproduce (observed / test case):
1) Start a streaming generation request that produces ~75-120s of output from redwood-4-8b model via SSE.
2) Midway through the stream, simulate an IP path change (e.g., client moves from WiFi to cellular or a short proxy restart that changes downstream source IP).
3) Client reconnects using the same auth token and reconnect logic; server accepts new connection.
4) Observe that stream resumes but the final closing metadata event or last sentence is missing; client SDK remains waiting for termination marker.

Observed behavior:
- Client receives reconnect ack and intermediate chunks after rejoin but never receives the terminal "end" event / final metadata envelope.
- Server logs show a new connection accepted for the same session-id but no application-level resume token is associated with it; the worker treats it as a fresh session and drains partial generator state without sending closing envelope.
- No 5xx from API gateway; connection lifecycle shows ALB connection rebind and a new TCP connection to edge.

Expected behavior:
- After reconnect, server should reattach to existing stream state (via resume token or explicit session id) and re-emit pending chunks including the final closing metadata so client completes cleanly.

Relevant logs/traces:
- Trace IDs from affected customer runs: trace-20260310-73a1, trace-20260310-73a2, trace-20260310-73b9.
- Edge/worker logs excerpt (anonymized):
  - edge-conn: accepted new socket from 54.210.12.77 for session:none token:missing
  - sidecar: session-mapper: affinity=ip-cookie mismatch, fallback=false
  - runtime: generator-id=gf-19f stop-detected: partial-flush, no-terminal-envelope
- Grafana dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-handovers?var=pool=redwood-dedicated-us-east-4 (spike in connection rebinds at 2026-03-10T14:43UTC)

Attachments:
- Customer-provided SDK log (trimmed): textflow_sse_log_20260310.txt
- PCAP from customer's edge-side proxy (shared privately)

Notes:
- Customer has implemented exponential reconnect/backoff and uses auth tokens per session; they do not supply an explicit session-id header by default (rely on token-derived mapping).
- Problem seems correlated with short ALB affinity cookie timeouts and NAT changes that present a new source IP to our edge within the same auth token window.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: ALB/NAT path change causes source IP mismatch and our session-mapper uses strict IP affinity when resume-token absent -> new socket not linked to generator state.

Hypothesis 2: Short affinity cookie triggers LB to route to a different edge instance; edge expects resume token in handshake but client SDK doesn't always send explicit session id, causing session to be treated as new.

Confirmed reproduction in staging with ip-move script that opens a second connection with different source port & NAT. Observed runtime generator state alive but detached from new connection (no terminal envelope).
Heap/worker dump analysis: generator state persisted (KV cache intact) and downstream flush executed but sidecar did not forward terminal envelope back to reattached socket due to missing mapping.
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround: customer to include explicit x-session-id header on streaming requests; this forces deterministic reattachment across IP/path changes. Engineering change: relax strict IP-only affinity in sidecar session-mapper and ensure resume-token attachment path is executed when a valid resume token or explicit session-id header is present. A small change merged to canary (PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2891). Plan: rollout to dedicated canary -> progressively to all dedicated pools in 48 hours; monitor truncated-streams rate.
